stem:
The Sun may be considered as a uniform sphere with a mass of 1.99 × 10³⁰ kg and a surface temperature of 580 K.

A probe with a mass of 2.63 kg moves in a straight line towards the Sun. When it is at a distance *x* from the centre of the Sun, the probe measures the gravitational field strength *g* due to the Sun and the radiant flux intensity *F* of radiation from the Sun.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: For the position of the probe where *x* = 1.47 × 10¹¹ m:

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: determine the gravitational potential energy *E*ₚ of the probe.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Show that, for any particular value of *x*, the numerical values of *g* and *F* are related by

$g = \frac{4πGM}{L}F$

where *M* is the mass of the Sun, *L* is the luminosity of the Sun and *G* is the gravitational constant.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Fig. 2.1 shows the variation of *g* with *F*.

[[fig:f1]]

Determine a value for the luminosity *L* of the Sun. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (c)(ii) to determine the radius *r* of the Sun.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A graph of g against F with a straight rising line from the origin.
